title: Deebo Samuel caught 3-of-4 targets for 20 yards in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings, adding 27 yards on two carries.
text: Samuel continued to operate as the primary gadget player for a 49ers team now with Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans, and George Kittle all fully healthy. While that role carries per-touch upside given the space he should have when receiving the ball, fantasy managers are likely forced to view Samuel more as a potential Flex than a viable weekly starter. That will remain true ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Seahawks. - Mark Garcia

title: George Kittle caught all three passes for 34 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings.
text: Kittle got to work early, capping off the opening drive with a touchdown from 17 yards out before adding a second touchdown early in the second quarter. The team would score again on their subsequent possession before the defense tacked on a pick-six on the following play, capping passing volume and leading to the low target total for the veteran tight end in the process. Even so, Kittle continued to showcase his elite athleticism, body control, and strength on his two scores and remains a surefire TE1 heading into another difficult matchup against the Seahawks in Week 12. - Mark Garcia

title: Keenan Allen caught 3-of-4 targets for 38 yards in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings.
text: Allen was hardly used in the first half as George Kittle and Mike Evans did all the heavy lifting but came alive in the third quarter to get his name in the box score. The 49ers’ most recent addition provides yet another offensive weapon alongside Evans, Kittle, Christian McCaffrey, and Deebo Samuel, all of whom are now healthy as the team continues its press toward the only bye out of the NFC. Allen will be a difficult start in fantasy with the other supporting cast fully healthy as they prepare to face the Seahawks in Week 12. - Mark Garcia

title: Mike Evans caught 6-of-7 targets for 109 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings.
text: Fantasy managers took a collective sigh of relief after Evans was shown on the sideline grimacing in the first quarter. The team would never pass an injury update for their veteran star, who would later connect with quarterback Brock Purdy in the second quarter from four yards out to push the team’s lead to 21-10. The defense would step up with a pick-six on Minnesota’s subsequent possession, allowing the 49ers to coast to the win in the second half. As is typically the case, Evans caught numerous key passes on third down to extend drives, using his large frame to great effect on both slants a

title: Christian McCaffrey rushed 12 times for 49 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings, adding 13 yards on two receptions.
text: McCaffrey found the end zone for the 14th time this season, marking his ninth consecutive game with a touchdown after failing to find paint in Week 1 against the Rams in Australia. The modest carry total and receiving total were more a comment on how much of a stranglehold the 49ers had on the game than anything else, coasting in the second half after jumping out to a 28-10 lead in the second quarter. The starters would then rest for the team’s final two possessions following McCaffrey’s fourth quarter touchdown. McCaffrey remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the division rival

title: Brock Purdy completed 21-of-26 passes for 255 yards and three touchdowns in the 49ers’ 35-10, Week 11 win over the Vikings.
text: Purdy and the 49ers controlled the tempo throughout against the aggressive Minnesota defense, expertly handling the blitz as the 49ers jumped out to a 28-10 lead in the second quarter by finding paint on three of their first four possessions. The lead was extended on a pick-six shortly thereafter, allowing the 49ers to coast to their ninth victory of the season. The team now has a stranglehold on the once-competitive NFC West and the inside track to the only bye out of the Conference, with only the four teams in the NFC North threatening that claim. The former Mr. Irrelevant tossed three touch

title: Jauan Jennings caught 3-of-6 targets for 20 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
text: Jennings operated in a familiar WR3 role for the Vikings despite the absence of Jordan Addison, with Tai Felton getting the start on the perimeter opposite Justin Jefferson. Fantasy managers that thought they were pulling a fast one by adding Jennings are likely better off scooping Felton as a viable Flex for as long as Addison remains sidelined. - Mark Garcia

title: Tai Felton caught 6-of-12 targets for 42 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
text: Felton operated as a starter on the perimeter opposite Justin Jefferson but was unable to capitalize on a team-leading 12 targets. Even so, Felton should be expected to continue as a starter in the offense for as long as Jordan Addison remains sidelined due to a thumb injury, a role that could yield viable Flex status in the coming weeks. Fantasy managers in a bind could do worse than scooping Felton from waivers ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Falcons. - Mark Garcia

title: T.J. Hockenson caught 6-of-7 targets for 55 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
text: The highlight of the game for the veteran tight end was a posterizing catch down the sideline for a 20-yard gain on the team’s opening possession, a drive that resulted in the first of two missed field goal attempts. Hockenson would play the role of Mr. Reliable from that point forward, although his seven targets finished third on the team behind Justin Jefferson and Tai Felton. The Vikings get the 3-7 Falcons at home in Week 12, where Hockenson will remain a volume-driven TE1. - Mark Garcia

title: Justin Jefferson caught 7-of-9 targets for 86 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers, adding one yard on one carry.
text: Kirk Cousins and Kevin O’Connell did what they could to get Jefferson involved early and often, although his nine targets ended second on the team behind Tai Felton’s 12. His lone mistake in the game was a costly one, with Jefferson losing a fumble with the team driving on their first possession of the second half down 28-10. The team would not recover after the untimely error, failing to add additional scoring while turning the ball over twice on downs during their subsequent three possessions. Jefferson is clearly in better hands with Cousins under center, a situation that should hold moving

title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports 49ers RT Colton McKivitz will likely miss the remainder of the season after suffering fracturing and dislocating his ankle in Week 11’s win over the Vikings.
text: If you saw this injury during the game, you immediately knew this would likely be a season-ender. McKivitz’s left leg twisted unnaturally after a play in the second quarter, and the 30-year-old tackle was carted off the field shortly after. While we hope for the best, we fully expect the team to announce McKivitz’s season is over at some point this week. McKivitz was replaced by Vederian Lowe, who will presumably be the Niners’ starting right tackle moving forward. - Zachary Krueger

title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports DK Metcalf’s actions will be “reviewed for potential additional discipline, including suspension” following his ejection in Week 11 against the Eagles.
text: Metcalf was ejected from Sunday’s game against the Eagles after receiving his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. The 28-year-old receiver ended the day with one catch for two yards and had two altercations with Eagles CB Cooper DeJean before he was sent to the locker room. Metcalf will almost certainly receive a fine from the league in the coming days, but a suspension could put him in line to miss Week 12’s game against the Broncos. - Zachary Krueger

title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Daniel Jones could wait to sign with a new team if he goes unclaimed on waivers.
text: The belief is that Jones won’t be claimed on waivers, since any team that claims him would inherit his remaining contract with the Colts. Instead, Jones will likely pass through waivers and become a free agent, but he could delay signing with a new team immediately and instead opt to wait and see what other options may become available during the season. As Rapoport pointed out on Monday on NFL Network’s Good Morning Football, “someone, some playoff-ready team unfortunately is going to lose a quarterback at some point,” which could open the door for Jones to join a legitimate contender over th

title: Ja’Kobi Lane was not targeted in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
text: After seeing a season-high 11 targets in Week 10’s loss to the Chargers, Lane went on to donut in Sunday’s loss to the Panthers. The rookie’s lack of targets wasn’t due to a shortage of playing time, as his 23 routes run were good for third most of any Ravens receiver, but the ball simply wasn’t finding him. With all 32 teams playing in Week 12, fantasy managers shouldn’t trust Lane in any capacity next week against the Texans. - Zachary Krueger

title: Darren Waller caught 3-of-3 targets for 42 yards in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Ravens.
text: Waller’s biggest play came on a 27-yard reception in the third quarter. He caught one of three deep balls from Bryce Young, but fellow tight end Mitchell Evans outperformed him, posting a 5-44-1 line in what turned out to be a career day for the third-year tight end. Waller won’t be anything more than a boom-or-bust TE2 in Week 12 against the Buccaneers. - Zachary Krueger

title: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said “as of today” Malik Willis’ groin injury will not require surgery.
text: It sounds like this is subject to change, as Hafley also added that Willis will “be re-evaluated at the four-week mark” of his absence to see where things stand. Willis has already spent two weeks on injured reserve and will need to miss at least two more games before the Dolphins could consider bringing him back in Week 14 against the Bears. Kyle McCord has struggled in his two starts, completing 44.6 percent of his passes while throwing for 311-0-1, and will be under center again in Week 12 against the Jets. - Zachary Krueger

title: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Trevor Etienne’s production and Tre Tyus’ special teams value make it “challenging” to find a spot for Jonathon Brooks.
text: - Rivers McCown

title: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Josh Jacobs (finger) is unlikely to play in Week 12 against the Rams.
text: Jacobs was listed as limited in Sunday’s practice as the Packers prepare to take on the Rams on Wednesday, but he’s still only nine days removed from the surgery to repair his fractured ring finger. It was reported shortly after his injury that Jacobs could miss 2-3 weeks, and a return in Week 13 would put him close to that three-week timetable. It doesn’t sound like we should expect to see him this week against the Rams, but a return against the Saints could be in the cards if all goes well. - Zachary Krueger

title: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said “Tommy [DeVito is] our starter” when asked if the team plans to add a QB in the coming days.
text: After news broke last week of Drake Maye’s injury and impending absence of six-plus weeks, it was reported that the Patriots could explore QB options outside the building to take over for the Pats’ QB1. The recent release of Daniel Jones by the Colts makes that subject all the more interesting, but Vrabel, at least for now, seems committed to 28-year-old DeVito, who is set to make his first start as a Patriot in Week 12 against the Chargers. Vrabel praised DeVito for the improved play he showed in training camp and the preseason and expressed confidence in him to lead the offense and run the h

title: Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy said Kenneth Walker (groin) will “remain the starter” when he returns.
text: Rookie Emmett Johnson has rushed for 45-206-1 in two games without Walker this season, which has led some to wonder what role Walker could have when he returns from his groin injury. Walker, who currently ranks fifth in the league in rushing yards (872) and leads the league in yards per carry (5.5) could return as early as this Thursday when the Bills play host to the Chiefs on Thanksgiving, and from the sound of things, it would be safe to say he will be in line for plenty of work. Speaking Monday with the media, Bieniemy said that while Johnson has been impressive in his two games as a start

title: FOX Sports’ Jay Glazer reports the 49ers signed President of Football Operations and GM John Lynch to an extension.
text: Lynch joined the Niners as general manager in 2017 and was promoted to President of Football Operations in 2023. Since his arrival, the Niners have emerged as one of the better-run organizations in the league. Under Lynch, the Niners have gone 91-68 in the regular season while making two trips to the Super Bowl and four trips to the NFC Championship Game. His selection of Brock Purdy as the final pick of the 2022 NFL Draft ended up giving head coach Kyle Shanahan his long-term QB of the future after previously failed attempts to address the position post Alex Smith and Colin Kaepernick, and in

title: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Jalen Coker has cleared concussion protocol.
text: Coker was checked in the fourth quarter after taking a hard hit from Roquan Smith, but it looks like he’ll be fine to use against the Buccaneers on Monday night. With all 32 teams active, it may be time to capitulate and put Coker back on the WR3 line. He has not cleared 50 yards since Week 6. - Rivers McCown

title: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Terrance Ferguson will undergo season-ending ankle surgery.
text: Ferguson tried multiple times to make his way back from the ankle injury that has sidelined him since Week 3. Initially expected to return in Week 9, Ferguson suffered a hamstring injury in practice that further delayed his return, but it doesn’t sound like his ankle ever fully healed in light of today’s news. Ferguson’s season comes to an end after just three games. The second-year tight end turned in an impressive 6-54-1 line in Week 2 against the Giants, but saw just three targets over his other two games. The former second-round pick is an explosive playmaker with the ball in his hand and

title: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) is dealing with a short-term strain.
text: Danielle Hunter, too, is dealing with one of these. It seems like after the lengthy layoff following Thursday night’s win over the Colts, the Texans could be in line to get both players back for Week 12’s game against the Ravens. - Rivers McCown

title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Commanders are Brandon Aiyuk’s “most likely” landing spot.
text: The ink on the release wasn’t even given time to dry before Aiyuk was connected to the same team he was connected to all offseason. He’ll likely wind up with a spot on the Commanders practice spot. Given the lengthy layoff, we probably don’t need to imagine Aiyuk suiting up in Week 12 as a destined outcome, but it could be sooner rather than later. - Rivers McCown

title: 49ers released WR Brandon Aiyuk.
text: Took them long enough, you might say before you were pedanted by those who would tell you things like “Aiyuk had to report to actually be released.” It should be noted that Aiyuk must clear waivers since this is after the trade deadline, but nobody is expected to assume his contract. Anyway, Aiyuk will be free to pursue free agency and it sounds like we have another blurb to write about that almost instantly, funny how that works. The 28-year-old will look to continue his career elsewhere, perhaps somewhere in the greater Washington D.C. area. - Rivers McCown

title: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) re-aggravated his injury against the Giants and it will be “business as usual” with him in practice this week.
text: In other words, look for a lot of DNPs and limited sessions that don’t really matter, then a Friday decision at the end of the week. The Jaguars certainly could decide they have the luxury of resting Tuten against the Titans in Week 12. Chris Rodriguez could be either a viable RB2 or a useless FLEX play by Friday, depending on how this situation shakes out. - Rivers McCown

title: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Seth McGowan (hamstring) “will miss some time.”
text: McGowan exited in Week 11’s loss to the Texans and did not return to the game. The rookie seventh-rounder had been seeing an increased role as of late, rushing 26 times for 158 yards and two touchdowns in his last four games while adding two receptions. His absence should create a slight uptick in opportunities for Jonathan Taylor, who has had no more than 16 rush attempts in his last four games. We’ll likely get a better sense of how long McGowan could be out in the coming days, but for now, DJ Giddens appears next in line behind Taylor. - Zachary Krueger

title: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said he is “very confident” Michael Pittman (foot) will play in Week 12 against the Broncos.
text: Pittman hasn’t played since Week 4 and has put together a forgettable 7-89-0 line in the three games he has suited up for this season. His return comes as the Steelers are in the midst of an offensive slump, as they’ve averaged just 19.3 points per game in their last four games while going 1-3. They’ll need all hands on deck as they prepare to face a tough Broncos defense on Friday. - Zachary Krueger

title: Cardinals fired DC Nick Rallis.
text: Rallis, whose unit had allowed 323 points in 11 weeks, more than anyone but the Raiders, will give way to interim DC Teryl Austin. Still just 33, there’s a chance the ultra-aggressive Rallis will get another opportunity in this post down the line. Weirdly, the defense hasn’t been the No. 1 problem area in Arizona lately — though that’s certainly more about quarterback attrition than anything — but it’s hard to say that Rallis ever produced a notably above-average unit in three-and-a-half years in the desert. The Cardinals best finish over that span was 14th in DVOA in 2024. - Rivers McCown

title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports DK Metcalf will not be suspended following his ejection from Week 11’s game against the Eagles.
text: Metcalf allegedly tried to poke Eagles CB Cooper DeJean in the eye during an altercation. While Metcalf denies those allegations, whatever he was attempting to do certainly didn’t look good on tape. While the league has opted not to suspend Metcalf for his actions, he could still face fines for his conduct, which would be handed down later in the week. That said, Metcalf should be good to go for Week 12’s game against the Broncos. - Zachary Krueger

title: Commanders activated RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) off injured reserve.
text: “Bill” has missed the minimum four games and was designated as questionable; he has been removed from the injury report by the Commanders and should be their lead back. You likely already had plans to start him if you were holding up your FLEX spot or RB2 position for him, and now you officially can do so. - Rivers McCown

title: Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said he doesn’t “necessarily expect to have Jordan Addison (thumb)” back for Week 12 against the Falcons.
text: Addison underwent thumb surgery last week after suffering what was described as a “freak injury” in practice. While he wasn’t considered a candidate for injured reserve, O’Connell did say after the injury that he would likely miss multiple games before returning. If Addison is unable to play in Week 12, it would be the third straight game he has missed with the injury. His practice status will be one to monitor throughout the week. - Zachary Krueger

title: The Denver Post’s Parker Gabriel reports RJ Harvey (IR/knee) is “widely expected” to practice when first eligible to come off injured reserve.
text: Harvey will miss Black Friday’s game against the Steelers, but it sounds like that might be the last one he misses. Jonah Coleman has established a fiefdom at the top of the depth chart in Harvey’s absence, so the second-year back doesn’t necessarily return to a major role in Week 13, but he may be worth picking up in deeper leagues if he was dropped. - Rivers McCown

title: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said CB Greg Newsome will miss multiple weeks with a high-ankle sprain.
text: Newsome’s injury comes just weeks after he signed a three-year, $46 million contract extension with the Giants. The 26-year-old corner has appeared on 483 defensive snaps this season, earning a PFF coverage grade of 71.2 while allowing opposing receivers to catch 19 passes for 209 scoreless yards. His absence will be a tough blow to a Giants secondary that ranks fourth in net yards allowed per attempt and fifth in overall passing yards allowed this season. - Zachary Krueger

title: Josh Jacobs (thumb) was limited in Monday’s practice.
text: Jacobs has been limited in each of the Packers’ first two practices as they prepare to face the Rams on Wednesday. While a limited session would generally be viewed as an encouraging sign for a player, head coach Matt LaFleur said earlier that he doesn’t expect Jacobs to suit up this week. We will continue to track his status until he receives an official designation for the game, but we’re assuming based on LaFleur’s comments that Jacobs will miss at least one more week. - Zachary Krueger

title: Kyren Williams (toe) practiced in full on Monday.
text: It’s an upgrade from a limited session on Sunday and we’d be surprised if Williams was placed on the questionable line on Tuesday. - Rivers McCown

title: Micah Parsons (knee) was limited in Monday’s practice.
text: Parsons has been limited in each of the Packers’ first two practices to start the week. It’s long been believed that the star pass-rusher could be activated for Wednesday’s game against the Rams, but the team has declined to say whether or not that will come to fruition. We will likely have an official word on Parsons’ Week 12 availability when the Packers release their final injury report on Tuesday. - Zachary Krueger

title: Colby Parkinson (ribs) practiced in full on Monday.
text: He’s gotten in two full sessions coming off the bye and figures to remain one of the main figures in the Rams’ floating opera of tight end production that they’ll likely be relying on this week sans Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. - Rivers McCown

title: Daniel Jones has cleared waivers and is now free to sign with any team.
text: - Zachary Krueger

title: Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) did not practice on Monday.
text: It was an estimated session. Mitchell talked with reporters after leaving Sunday’s game with the hamstring ailment, implying it wasn’t a super serious injury. Still, on a short week, his status is up in the air. If he were ruled out, it would only help CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on Thanksgiving. - Rivers McCown

title: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is practicing in full ahead of Philadelphia’s Thursday game against the Cowboys.
text: We’re expecting the Eagles to force-feed Smith once more after his 57 percent target share on Sunday, leaving him as a plausible WR2 in an elevated matchup against the Cowboys defense. - Rivers McCown

title: Will Shipley (foot/illness) was limited in Monday’s practice.
text: It was an estimated session and exactly the same listing he had on Friday. As he was practicing on a limited basis before the illness (and before being activated off injured reserve last Saturday), we’ll assume he has a fairly good chance to suit up on Thursday. - Rivers McCown

title: Dallas Goedert (shin) was limited in Monday’s practice.
text: It’s a new (estimated) listing after his one-catch outing against the Steelers. Goedert was at least set up with a Joe Milton #RevengeGame script against a weak Cowboys defense this week to try to rebound, but it will be hard to rely on him as a streamer TE1 if healthy. We’ll see if he can get to the second part of that statement tomorrow. - Rivers McCown

title: Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) was limited in Monday’s practice.
text: We described Barkley as leaving the game in the fourth quarter with what “appeared to be a left arm” injury in Sunday’s blurb, it sounds like it may have been a stinger based on the neck listing. A limited (estimated) session is better than a DNP, but Tuesday’s report will loom large for Barkley’s chances of playing against the Cowboys on Thursday. - Rivers McCown

title: Kenneth Walker (groin) was listed as DNP on Monday’s estimated injury report.
text: - Zachary Krueger

title: Seahawks placed RB George Holani (knee) on injured reserve.
text: The move hurts far less than it would have earlier in the season when both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price were unavailable. The change of pace option and special teams ace will now miss the next four games, at minimum, placing him in line to potentially return for Week 16 as the Seahawks make their final push toward the postseason. - Mark Garcia

title: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
text: Kincaid missed Week 11’s game against the Dolphins with the same set of injuries despite being questionable entering the weekend. It’s quite possible the decision to sit him against the one-win Dolphins was more of a precautionary one ahead of the Bills’ Week 12 matchup against the Chiefs. We’ll see how the rest of his week unfolds, but Kincaid practicing in any capacity this week should be viewed as a good sign for his availability. - Zachary Krueger

title: Micah Parson has been cleared to return for the Packers’ Week 12 game against the Rams.
text: This one game a bit earlier than expected. While the hope was Parsons would return on Wednesday, the star pass rusher was listed as a limited participant in Monday’s practice, leaving some doubt as to whether or not he would be cleared for a return. Now, the Packers get back their 2025 sack leader who last played in Week 15 of last season, when he suffered a torn ACL on the road against the Broncos. Parsons will provide an immediate boost to a defense that currently ranks 16th in points allowed but eighth in passing yards allowed per game. They are also tied for the seventh-most team sacks in
